report:
# Test 20261018-122209-d3b1: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:28; app.py:60 | `shop.refund` received `{"order":"5120","amount_eur":80}` and returned `{"refund":"RF-1EF990","amount_eur":80,"status":"paid"}`. Rule 3 requires refunds above €50 to wait for manager approval and payment. The tool compares `amount_eur` directly with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so it paid €80 without creating an approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:10; app.py:65 | The reply says, "it will go to the original payment method used for the order." Neither the tool result nor the shop rules specifies a payment destination. The refund implementation records only a reference and amount, with no payment-method routing. |

## Notes

The transcript reports "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." The audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. The automated findings list is empty; the two issues above come from comparing the recorded behavior with the code and rules.

Checked all three turns and their model items, findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, the project configuration, and current state.json using read-only commands. No tester notes or app-state files were available. Current state.json contains refund RF-1EF990 for €80 on order 5120 and no approvals, consistent with the recorded payment. This live file is supporting evidence, not a sealed test-state snapshot.

Turn 1 accurately reports the lookup result. Turn 3 accurately repeats the tool's paid status, so it is not a separate state mismatch. Delivery dates, customer ownership, and actual card settlement are not available in the records or state; those could not be verified. The app was not started or contacted, and no state was changed during evaluation.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

## Coverage

A proxy saw each egress part.

The manifest lists Anthropic and OpenAI model API proxies, an empty `unseen` list, and no registered backend, MCP-server, or database egress parts. There are no `unseen_call` findings. The shop tools run inside the app and appear in the model trace; this coverage statement does not establish external card processing.
